---
title: "Study 05 — MACE-OFF23 surrogate"
subtitle: "MACE-OFF23 (small) vs GFN2-xTB · droplets · off-the-shelf, no fine-tuning"
---

The main direction: can a machine-learned potential carry the workflow to larger
systems? We compare **MACE-OFF23** (DFT-trained, ωB97M-D3BJ) against GFN2-xTB —
first on static forces/energies, then in actual MD.

## Static: forces & energies track closely

On the droplet trajectories, force components correlate at **r ≈ 0.99** and
relative energies agree to **~2–3 meV/atom**. And the scaling is the prize: MACE
is ~linear while xTB is ~O(N³), so MACE's relative cost falls across the size
ladder — by 150 atoms they are equal, and beyond that the MLIP wins.

| n | atoms | force r | force RMSE | rel-E | MACE cost vs xTB |
|---|:-----:|:-------:|:----------:|:-----:|:----------------:|
| 20 | 60 | 0.992 | 0.185 eV/Å | 3.3 meV/atom | 2.5× |
| 30 | 90 | 0.992 | 0.190 eV/Å | 2.5 meV/atom | 1.6× |
| 50 | 150 | 0.991 | 0.198 eV/Å | 2.3 meV/atom | **1.0×** |

![Force parity (left) — tight along the diagonal, r ≈ 0.99. Relative energies
(right) track frame-by-frame.](assets/force_parity.png){width=420}

## Dynamics: same droplet structure in MD

Running unbiased NVT MD with each potential, MACE-OFF23 reproduces the droplet
**structure**, not just static forces — the go-ahead for MACE-driven sampling.

| | O–O 1st peak | R_g | mean coordination | condensed? |
|---|:-----------:|:---:|:-----------------:|:----------:|
| GFN2-xTB | 2.83 Å | 3.78 ± 0.07 Å | 4.01 | yes |
| MACE-OFF23 | 2.83 Å | 3.85 ± 0.05 Å | 3.72 | yes |

![O–O pair distribution (left) is essentially identical — same H-bond peak at
2.83 Å; droplet-size distributions (right) overlap.](assets/md_structure_n20.png){width=680}

::: {.callout-note}
## Off-the-shelf, no fine-tuning
MACE-OFF23 is DFT-trained, *not* fit to xTB — so this is two independent methods
agreeing, and where they differ MACE is presumably the more accurate one.
Fine-tuning would be the lever only if we later want it matched to a specific
reference.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Throughput needs a config pass
The MACE MD ran anomalously slow here (~2817 ms/step over a ~4 h run) versus
~75 ms/step in the static benchmark — likely CPU float64 + torch threading.
Before scaling MACE MD / metadynamics up: float32 inference, thread pinning, or
GPU. Structure is validated; production speed is a separate task.
:::

## Next

- Fix MACE MD throughput, extend the size ladder past n=50.
- **MACE-driven metadynamics** (ASE/PLUMED) — which unlocks biasing along proper
  collective variables. **Which CV** is the open question: coordination numbers,
  per-O O–H (proton transfer), tetrahedral order, or a learned CV.
